column1: # Two IOC sea-level rows retired 2026-10-24 as duplicates of one endpoint.
# www.ioc-sealevelmonitoring.org/service.php?query=stationlist was registered
# FOUR times. Measured live 2026-10-23 with the engine's own agent:
#   showall=all   HTTP 200  2,389,277 B  2,349 rows  2,039 byte-distinct
#   showall=a     HTTP 200  1,966,120 B  1,924 rows
#   (no showall)  HTTP 200  1,966,121 B  1,924 rows
# showall=a and no-showall are the same response, so the service IGNORES an
# unrecognised value and serves the default list. That is why lint-sources and
# the 531-pair dup baseline never grouped these: check_dup_endpoint keys on
# host+path+QUERY textually, and a parameter the SERVER discards still
# distinguishes two rows to a string comparison.
# Candidate keys against distinct whole records, showall=all (2,039):
#   Code                                    1,766
#   sensorid                                1,648   (119 NULL)
#   Code+sensor+sensorid                     1,766
#   Code+sensor+sensorid+updatedata          1,867   <- the surviving row's key
# The 2,349 -> 1,867 gap is CORRECT dedupe, not loss: the 115 colliding groups
# differ only in observations/first/last, counters that advance every minute.
# Widening the key would mint a fresh uid every run and grow the table without
# bound. Measured before repairing, per rule 4b.
# KEPT: ioc-sea-level-stations (sources/mar_ioc_sea_level_stations.c) - the
#   sensor-level read, keyed code|sensor|sensorid|updatedata, carries the gauge
#   position and lasttime as published_at.
# KEPT: ioc-sealevel-stations (sources/geoeo_ioc_sealevel.c) - a different
#   RECORD GRANULARITY (one row per station, sensors folded into sensor_count)
#   on the default list, keyed on Code. Not a duplicate of the above.
# CAUTION on the per-pass numbers in the evidence column (added 2026-10-24).
# "stored 1,763 of 2,385" and "stored 1,341 of 1,960" are readings from the
# 2026-08-24 source-health and 2026-09-04 collision sweeps, and both PREDATE
# the in-page collision guard that content-hashes records colliding inside one
# page. These two rows are SINGLE-PAGE reads -- service.php returns the whole
# list in one response, no cursor, no next link -- so under the guard a
# surviving collapse on them would prove the records were byte-identical, i.e.
# correct dedupe, not loss. Nobody re-measured them after the guard landed.
# So: do NOT read this removal as recovering ~1,238 records/pass. It removes a
# duplicated REQUEST and duplicated STORAGE, which is certain, and it removes a
# row whose name misdescribed its endpoint. Whether either row was still
# losing records was unmeasured, and the honest answer is that it probably was
# not. The grounds for retiring them do not depend on it.
# Registry count 57,529 -> 57,527; both floors re-recorded.
